## Teaching points

1. Pain followed by a unilateral vesicular eruption in one dermatome is characteristic. Ask about ocular symptoms and immune status.
2. Assess distribution, immune status and ocular or neurologic symptoms rather than assuming every vesicular rash is uncomplicated.
3. Early oral antiviral treatment is appropriate for this older adult with a fresh localized rash; check renal function and dosing context.
4. Cover lesions and avoid exposing susceptible high-risk contacts until crusted; analgesia may improve sooner than the rash.
